transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
Another candidate backed by the Democratic Socialists of America has prevailed in the
midterms.
City Council member Nithya Raman will be the next mayor of Los Angeles, according to a
call from the Associated Press.
She defeated mayoral incumbent Karen Bass.
Raman says the city had reached a breaking point and jumped into the race just hours
before the filing deadline.
Passes the first L.A. mayor in two decades to lose a bid for re-election, preceded by
criticism of her response to the deadly Palisades fire.
The mayor says in a statement that she called Raman to congratulate her and is committed
to a seamless transition.
Texas Democrats are celebrating a blue wave in the state.
That includes the election of the state's first Latina governor, Gina Inajosa.
In her first press conference, since she defeated Republican governor Greg Abbott, Inajosa responded
to reports that state GOP opponents might try to undermine her authority.
I would hope that elected leaders from both parties don't get in the way of the progress
we can make together to deliver for working people.
That is our obligation as leaders in this state.
Meanwhile, NPR has spoken to Georgia's governor-elect Heesha Lance Bottoms about her top priorities
once she takes office, such as housing and health care.
With our health care cuts, nine rural hospitals have closed, so many of our Bragg counties
have been hit harder than even our urban centers on issues related to health care.
Bottoms is the first black woman in the nation to be elected governor.
Well, stocks tumbled again today, erasing the gains that followed the midterm elections.
NPR's Scott Horsley has an update.
The sell-off in stocks began in the tech sector, then rapidly spread to the broader market.
Investors were already having second thoughts about high-priced stocks tied to the artificial
intelligence boom.
Those doubts were amplified on Tuesday, when voters in many parts of the country showed
their opposition to data centers.
Stocks initially rallied after the election.
Investors often welcomed divided government as a check on the excesses of both parties.
But that early enthusiasm quickly evaporated.
Some investors shifted money into government bonds, which pushed yields lower.
The average rate on a 30-year mortgage dipped below 7.2 percent, although that's still almost
a full percentage point higher than this time last year.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
President Trump's attorneys were scheduled to be in court today to attempt to clear his
name in a hush money conviction case.
More than two years ago, a New York jury found him guilty on 34 felony counts of falsifying
business records to conceal payment to an adult film actress ahead of the 2016 election.
At the close, the Dow Jones Industrial Average was down more than 1,600 points, or more than
3 percent, you're listening to NPR News.
At a White House event, First Lady Melania Trump says she wants to see an enduring ceasefire
in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
Here's NPR's Charles Maines.
The local ceasefire was limited to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshki, and surrounding areas in
southern Ukraine, a pause in fighting that allowed humanitarian aid to reach residents,
several hundred of whom were later evacuated.
Mrs. Trump said she hoped the Oleshki mission would serve as an example going forward.
Together we can create something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire.
Russian and Ukrainian officials were both on hand for the event, including a Kremlin
envoy who said Russian president Vladimir Putin supported the First Lady's efforts.
Yet Putin has repeatedly rejected previous U.S. ceasefire proposals, instead arguing for
a comprehensive peace deal that hinges in part on Ukraine relinquishing large parts
of its territory.
Charles Maines, NPR News, Moscow.
Ex-Zit polls examining the religious vote in the midterm show increasing support for
Democrats among those with no religious affiliation.
President Peirce Jason DeRose.
Nearly eight in ten religiously unaffiliated voters went for Democrats during the midterms.
According to an exit poll conducted by NBC News, Catholic voters were evenly divided
between Republicans and Democrats this year after breaking for GOP candidates in 2024.
Support for Democrats among Jewish voters appears to be softening.
A CNN exit poll found that about seven in ten went for Democrats in the midterms, while
the number was nearly eight in ten two years ago.
Just prior to the election, Pew Research found that the economy was the overriding issue
for voters, regardless of religious affiliation.
That's Jason DeRose.
It's NPR.
